body.title: feat(rules): rule schema, YAML loader, --rules and test harness
body.body:
## Summary

This PR builds the core of the rule engine for milestone M4. It loads rules from YAML, checks them, embeds the built-in rules in the binary, and adds `mcpmoat scan --rules <dir>` for extra rules. It also adds the test harness that makes `go test` fail when a built-in rule has no tests.

Rules are loaded and checked. They are not applied to scan results yet. The scan output is the same as before, and the "no rules applied" notice stays.

- **#33 Rule schema and YAML loader.** New package `internal/rules` with `Rule`, `Match`, `Case`, `LoadError`, `Validate`, `Parse` and `Set`. Decoding is strict. It adds one module, `go.yaml.in/yaml/v3` v3.0.5. The repo owner approved this module before it was added.
- **#34 Embedded rules and `--rules`.** Built-in rules are embedded with `go:embed` from a small root package, `rules/`. `rules/MOAT-T1-003.yaml` is the first built-in rule. The other rule issues add more. `mcpmoat scan --rules <dir>` adds extra `*.yaml` and `*.yml` files.
- **#41 Test harness.** `go test` fails when a built-in rule has no `should_match` case, no `should_not_match` case, no risk text or no remediation text. `CONTRIBUTING.md` documents the final format.
- **#32 `docs/competitors.md`.** Five tools, with a source link for every claim. `alexar76/warden` exists and is the closest competitor. The `mcp-lock` row is a best guess, because several repositories use that name. The document lists the other candidates.

Decisions the repo owner confirmed: the loader is lenient and the built-in harness is strict, test cases live inline in the rule YAML, and the competitor research uses the web.

Not in this PR on purpose:

- Regex compilation and matchers (#35).
- Native heuristics (#36).
- The ignore list (#40).
- More rules.
- Applying rules to scan results.

The place where matchers will plug in is `Matcher` and `Compiler` in `internal/rules/seam.go`. `TestBuiltinRulesCases` is skipped on purpose until #35 provides a compiler. Then two small changes are needed: return the compiler from `builtinCompiler()` in `builtin_test.go`, and pass `WithCompiler(...)` in `cmd/mcpmoat/scan_rules.go`.

Closes #33
Closes #34
Closes #41
Closes #32

## PRD references

FR-07, FR-08, FR-09 (schema part), NFR-05, NFR-07, and PRD section 13 (competitors).

## Security

Rule files are untrusted input. A cloned repo or a `--rules` folder can ship them. What this PR does about it:

- **Hard limits.** 64 KiB per file, 1000 files, 5000 rules, and caps on list sizes and text sizes.
- **Error caps.** At most 20 errors per file, 100 per folder and 100 per rule set. Each cap ends with one summary line.
- **YAML bombs.** Anchors, aliases, deep nesting and huge node counts are rejected before any field is decoded.
- **No silent drops.** A null item in any list is an error. Before the fix, `should_match: [~]` loaded and lost the case without a message.
- **Reference URLs.** ASCII `http` or `https` only. They are never fetched.
- **Terminal safety.** All rule-derived text goes through `termsafe` before it reaches the terminal. This covers control characters, C1 controls, bidi controls and format characters.
- **Folder access.** `os.OpenRoot` confines reads to the folder. Symlinks and non-regular files are refused.
- **No side effects.** The new code makes no network call, starts no process and writes no file.

Two security reviews and a three-agent review (security, logic, quality) ran on this branch. Every Critical and Should-fix finding was fixed:

- A hostile rules folder made `scan --rules` use 2.2 GB of memory and 47 seconds, and print about 10 million stderr lines. Fixed with the error caps.
- Null list items were dropped silently.
- Reference URLs accepted invisible and bidi characters.
- `params` without `heuristic` and a blank `heuristic` passed validation.
- `NewSet` printed one error for every clashing rule, which bypassed the folder cap.

## Known limits and follow-ups

These Minor and Nit findings are known and not fixed here.

Security-tagged:

- A FIFO swapped in between the directory listing and the open can block `--rules`. The attacker needs write access to the rules folder. The cheapest fix is `O_NONBLOCK` through `root.OpenFile`.
- `Match.Params` has no type or size caps. This belongs to #36.
- `ReadDir` lists every entry before the 1000-file cap applies.
- Ignored files such as `x.YAML`, and an empty rules folder, give no notice.
- Lookalike ASCII rule IDs are allowed, for example `moat-t1-003` next to `MOAT-T1-003`.
- The regex compiler is not wired into `--rules` yet. A bad regex does not exit 2 until #35.
- When `LoadDir` reports errors, `NewSet` does not run. An ID clash shows only after the file errors are fixed.
- `RunCases` does not recover a panicking `Matcher`.

Correctness and polish:

- In the folder-cap summary, "N files not checked" can be off by one when the cut file is the last one, and it reads "1 files".
- `Validate` errors are not sorted in file order.
- A decode error inside `match` names `match`, not the key.
- The risk text check misses `\v` and `\f`.

Quality follow-ups, not blocking:

- The error-cap bookkeeping in `parse.go` (`errList`, `mergeByPosition`) could be one stable sort.
- The terminal-safety test helper is copied in six test files.
- The in-process and end-to-end `--rules` tests overlap.
- `show` and `displayText`, and `maxDocumentedRiskRunes` and `maxRiskRunes`, are duplicates.
- `Option` and `WithCompiler` are machinery for a single option.

Not caused by this PR: `govulncheck` reports GO-2026-6809 in the Go toolchain (`crypto/x509`, fixed in go1.27.3). It is reached through `internal/inspect/httpclient.go`. `go.mod` still says `toolchain go1.27.2`, so the `govulncheck` step in CI will fail until the toolchain line is bumped in a separate change.

## Go notes for the reader

- **`go:embed` from a root package.** `go:embed` cannot use `..` in a path. So `internal/rules` cannot embed the repo-root `rules/` folder. The small package `rules/embed.go` embeds `*.yaml` and exports it as `FS`. `internal/rules` imports it with the alias `builtinrules`.
- **`os.OpenRoot`.** `LoadDir` opens the folder with `os.OpenRoot` and reads through `root.FS()`. Reads cannot leave the folder, even through a symlink.
- **Fixed sentinel errors and `errors.Is`.** Messages that reach the user come from fixed error values and typed `Reason` constants, not from library error text. Tests use `errors.Is` to check the cause.
- **`yaml.Node` first pass.** `Parse` decodes into `yaml.Node` first. A node knows its line and column. That is how errors say `file:4:11`. Fields are then decoded one by one, so a type error names the field and not a Go type.
- **Functional option `WithCompiler`.** `Builtin(opts ...Option)` and `LoadDir(dir, opts ...Option)` accept options. `WithCompiler` is the only one. It is the hook for #35.
- **Table tests and fuzzing.** Tests are table-driven. `FuzzParse` feeds random input to `Parse` and checks fixed rules: no panic, errors are bounded, and error text is safe.

## Testing

- [x] `go test ./...` (run as `go test -race -shuffle=on -count=1 ./...`: all packages pass; one expected skip, `TestBuiltinRulesCases`, issue #35)
- [x] `go vet ./...`
- [x] `golangci-lint run` (0 issues)
- [x] `gofmt -l .` prints nothing
- [x] `go mod tidy -diff` prints nothing, and `go mod verify` passes
- [x] `go test -fuzz=FuzzParse -fuzztime=30s ./internal/rules/` found no crash
- [x] Mutation checks: removing the error caps, the null-item checks, the ASCII reference check and the blank-heuristic check each make tests fail
- [x] Manual run: `scan --no-connect --rules testdata/rules/invalid` exits 2 and prints `testdata/rules/invalid/bad-severity.yaml:4:11: field severity: invalid value: ...`
- [ ] `govulncheck ./...` reports the known toolchain finding GO-2026-6809 (see above). It reports nothing else.

## Checklist

- [x] New rules have `should_match` and `should_not_match` cases
- [x] No new network calls or telemetry. One new module, `go.yaml.in/yaml/v3`, approved by the repo owner
- [x] No secrets in output, logs, fixtures or test data
- [x] Docs updated if behaviour or flags changed (`CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/competitors.md`)

## Release Notes

- **`mcpmoat scan --rules <dir>`** (new flag): loads extra rule files (`*.yaml` and `*.yml`) from a folder, in addition to the built-in rules. It does not look in subfolders. A rule file that is not valid stops the scan with exit code 2. The message names the file, the line and the field. A rule ID that is the same as a built-in rule ID is also an error.
- **Rule `MOAT-T1-003`** (hidden actions): it is now built into the binary. Rules are not applied to scan results yet, so scan output does not change in this release.
- Internal: new `internal/rules` package with the rule format, loader and test harness. Built-in rules are embedded from `rules/`. The rule file format is documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. New `docs/competitors.md`.
